chapter_theme: Natrinai 381-400, the close of the anthology: waiting through the rains (Avvaiyar's rain like Anji's gifts, the lightning of Alankanam), hiding grief for the man's good name, the friend's pressure for marriage (beauty demanded back, the night path's dangers, the girl's tears at sunset), creatures that guard and feed their mates as pledges of a husband's care, the eloping man's joy, the woman who fears a next birth only for the forgetting it would bring, and the courtesan's boasts and praise.

comparisons.tenor: the rain that has settled in and keeps pouring

381.reading: In the season of rain the woman says she is neither dead nor truly alive; her heart trembles without rest like the fresh shoots of a kadamba whose roots lie bared on the eroding bank of a forest stream, and she cannot bear the pain, for the rain has settled in and darkened the sky as steadily as Neduman Anji, kind of heart and famous far, keeps giving away chariots from his seat.
381.nuance: Avvaiyar turns her own patron's unstinting gifts into the image of a rain that will not stop: the plenty that delights a bard is, for a woman waiting through the season, a torment that keeps on coming.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை ஆற்றாளாகிய தலைமகள் பருவ வரவின்கண் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the settled rains of the promised season

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names no addressee; the friend is assumed

iraicchi.act: the birds, fed, go back together to their nests at evening
iraicchi.sense: even the birds come home together at nightfall, while he stays away without a thought of her

382.reading: At evening in the shore grove, as the backwater swells, the blue neythal close their petals and the sea beats without end, and the birds, fed on fish, go back together to their nests, the woman tells her friend that though she suffers here while he stays away without a thought of her, she must hide it even if her life goes, because the slander his enemies would spread would shame the lord of the cool shore.
382.nuance: Her reason for silence is not her own modesty but his name: concealment becomes a service to the absent man.

colophon.thurai: ஒருவழித் தணந்த காலத்துப் பொழுதுபட ஆற்றாளாகி நின்ற தலைமகளைத் தோழி ஆற்றுவிக்கல்லாள் ஆயினாட்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the shore grove at evening

383.reading: The friend, having seen the path, tells the man of the high hill that he seems gracious but is not, coming at the dreadful midnight along a road buried in thick darkness, where thunder routs the snakes and a tiger, its striped cubs like a garland of vengai flowers and its mate hungry after birth, smashes a tusker's spotted face, kills it and roars like thunder.
383.nuance: The tiger hunting for a mate that has just given birth is the very danger the man walks into; the reproach is a way of saying his love endangers both of them.

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, tiger and tusker of the hill at midnight

iraicchi.act: the male dove gleans paddy from a ruined village to feed his mate, weak after laying
iraicchi.sense: the man taking her across the waste means to provide for her as the dove provides for his mate

384.reading: Eloping with the girl, the man tells his heart to look: on the path through a far land without forts, where the red-legged dove gathers spilt paddy from an old village laid waste by kings to feed his mate, slow and spent after laying in a brushwood nest on the forked kalli of the salt waste, the new gold-like vengai flowers have spread for her to walk on, she, the innocent one, who was the cure when he suffered after casting off shame.
384.nuance: The cure he once needed is now walking beside him, and the waste itself seems to lay down flowers for her.

colophon.thurai: உடன் போகாநின்றான் மலிந்து தன் நெஞ்சிற்குச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the salt waste and ruined villages of the road

385.reading: The speaker, probably the friend, tells the man that the day is over, the flowers have closed, the tortoise with its young and the crab have crowded into their holes on the reeking shore of the curving backwater, and the birds, their labour of seeking food done, rest in the trees with their chicks, so it is no hour for him to come alone; the rest of the poem is lost.
385.nuance: Every creature named is at home with its young; the unmarried man alone is abroad, and the friend's list is already a demand that he give her a home.

thinai_evidence.note: crab, tortoise and backwater of the shore

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon has no thurai; speaker and addressee are inferred from the poem

386.reading: The friend tells the woman that when the man of the land where a small-eyed, great-tempered boar gorges on the hunters' millet and then sleeps on the bamboo slope unafraid of the tiger in its rock-cleft lair offered to swear a dread oath by the god, she marvelled, knowing that men of his kind do not stoop to such things; yet he came, humbly, saying 'wedding', so that their small stony village shone.
386.nuance: The boar that eats the guarded millet and sleeps unafraid near the tiger could be read as the lover who took the girl under her kin's eyes, but no part of the poem maps it to a second correspondence, so it is left as scene.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தையின் மறுத்தந்த தலைமகற்கு வாயில் நேர்ந்த தோழி தலைமகளை முகம்புகுவல் என முற்பட்டாள் தலைமகள் மாட்டு நின்ற பொறாமை நீங்காமை அறிந்து பிறிது ஒன்றன்மேல் வைத்து பாவியேன் இன்று பேதைமை செய்தேன் எம்பெருமாட்டி குறிப்பு உணர்ந்து வழிபடுவேனாவேன்மன்னோ எனச்சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: boar, millet and hunters of the hill slope

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi

occasion.words: பரத்தையின் மறுத்தந்த தலைமகற்கு வாயில் நேர்ந்த தோழி

thurai_akam.note: the poem itself reads as the friend recalling the oath and the wedding

comparisons.tenor: the lightning of the rain cloud

387.reading: The friend tells the woman, whose curled hair and long arms lose their old beauty day by day, that the man who crossed the hard waste of forked tracks barred by the bows of untaught Mazhavar will come: look, the clamorous cloud has ringed the tall hill and pours heavy rain, flashing like swords drawn from their sheaths in the camp of Chezhiyan, whose spear-bearing army won the war and camped in terror at Alankanam.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை மெலிந்த தலைமகளைத் தோழி பருவம் காட்டி வற்புறீஇயது

thinai_evidence.note: waiting, with the rain shown as the sign of his return

388.reading: Asked how pallor could come to her fine brow, the woman says the lord of the cool shore never leaves her small heart, the shore where fishermen in sturdy boats, with harpoons on strong ropes, light bright torches, hunt at midnight, bring fish at dawn, heap it in the grove and, in the striped shade of the tall punnai, drink honey-fragrant toddy with their kin and rejoice greatly.
388.nuance: The fishermen's great rejoicing is set against her 'small heart': his shore is all feasting, and the only place he stays is inside her.

colophon.thurai: வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாகிய தோழிக்குத் தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறமாகச் சொல்லியது மனையுள் வேறுபடாது ஆற்றினாய் என்றாற்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: fishermen, punnai and the sea's catch

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names the hero as overhearer; the speaker is read as the heroine

389.reading: With the man listening, the friend tells the girl that the vengai has put out its tiger-striped blossoms and the falls on the honeyed hill shine like gems, their mother has looked on them kindly, and their father, going off after game with his young servants whose arrows split elephants' faces, has told her to guard the heavy-eared millet the small parrots raid; so let their bond be a loving passion with the man of the land where the dust the jungle fowl and its mate scratch up on the old upland glitters with gold.
389.nuance: The father's command to guard the millet is, without his knowing it, the opening of the daytime meeting place; the friend says it aloud so that the man will know the chance.

colophon.thurai: பகற்குறி வந்து ஒழுகாநின்ற காலத்துத் தலைமகன் கேட்பச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, millet and parrots of the hill

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon names only the overhearer; the speaker is read as the friend

390.reading: The speaker says she would like to go to the festival wearing a leaf skirt of white water lilies from the fields around Venni of generous Killi, where vaalai fish flash like swords and the otter of the pond takes its morning sleep; if the lord of the rich town sees her he can hardly fail to take her, and if he does, the fine arms of many women, like the bamboo of the hill of Mudiyan of true word and hill-like elephants, will be pitiable and waste.
390.nuance: The boast is made to be overheard: the speaker parades her power over the man to those who carry word to the house.

colophon.thurai: பாங்கு ஆயின வாயில் கேட்ப நெருங்கிச் சொல்லியது தலைமகள் தோழிக்கு உரைப் பாளாய் வாயிலாகப் புக்கார் கேட்ப சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: field, water lily and pond of the river plain

thurai_akam.speaker: parathai
thurai_akam.note: the colophon does not name the speaker; the boast fits the courtesan; the overhearers are the go-betweens

thurai_akam.speaker: thalaivi
thurai_akam.note: the overhearers are those who came as go-betweens

391.reading: The friend tells the girl not to weep, for he will give up the journey: who would leave for wealth, even to win the Ezhil hill in Nannan's good gold-bearing Konkanam, where bright-bangled women gather gold from the cool track the dark-horned buffalo opened after grazing the cold creepers of a grove dappled like a tiger's spots, and make her great rain-dark eyes, like a water-dripping kuvalai, fill with tears?

colophon.thurai: பிரிவு உணர்த்தப்பட்டு ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வற்புறுத்தியது வரைவு உணர்த்தியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: a journey for wealth announced and to be given up

392.reading: The friend wishes the lovers knew their good house in the small town fenced with palmyra, where the shock-haired boys who cried at home when their shark-spearing father went off to the bird-loud sea without taking them are cheered by the warm swelling flesh of sweet palm fruit; those who came proudly and turned back seem to suffer with the shore grove, but they, of very great love, may yet clear the lonely sorrow of the midnight.
392.nuance: The boys consoled with palm fruit while their father is at sea are a small model of the girl, comforted with promises while her lover is away.

colophon.thurai: இரவுக்குறி முகம்புக்கது வரைவு நீட ஆற்றாளாய தலைமகளைத் தோழி வரைவு உணர்த்தி வற்புறுத்தியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: shark-fishing, sea and palmyra of the shore village

iraicchi.act: the tusker raids the millet, braving the hunter's firebrand, to restore his mate weak after calving
iraicchi.sense: the man who braved the night roads will now provide for her as a husband

393.reading: The friend asks whether, now that their people have agreed to give the girl to the man who came truly to marry and they are spared the dangers of his night visits, the family will accept him when they see their lover come as a new man and her bridal shyness, he of the land where a young tusker, wild with joy, seizes the curved millet to restore his mate weak from calving, and the firebrand the hunter hurls at him lights the bamboo slope like a shooting star.

thinai_evidence.note: elephant, hunter and the bamboo slope

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon gives only the occasion; the speaker addresses the bride as நின்

394.reading: Onlookers on the waste road tell the returning man that he went, bless him, in the harsh cold season, his tall jewelled chariot ringing with bells and its wheels rattling over the hard gravel, through a forest crowded with trees where an owl on a withered nyemai calls as sweetly as a goldsmith tapping, and that since the cloud has poured midway, the sandal paste on his chest must be cool and fragrant; they grieve for her.
394.nuance: Strangers on the road can only imagine the welcome: the rain that cools him is the sign she has been waiting through.

colophon.thurai: வினை முற்றி மறுத்தராநின்ற தலைமகனை இடைச் சுரத்துக் கண்டார் சொல்லியது வன்சொல்லால் குறை நயப்பித்த தோழி தந்து அளித்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: the man returning in the rains after his work

395.reading: The friend asks the lord of the shore who he is to them, a mere stranger, and whether that is how things stand between them: he did not desire their girl, who is like Maanthai on the sea, loud at evening when cows come home after feeding on the flowers dropped by girls who dive in waves that roar like the drums in Kuttuvan's king-slaying battle; so let him give back her beauty and go.
395.nuance: 'Give back her beauty and go' is a legal formula of restitution: the friend treats the man's courtship as a taking that must be repaid by marriage or undone.

colophon.thurai: நலம் தொலைந்தது எனத் தலைவனைத் தோழி கூறி வரைவு கடாயது

thinai_evidence.note: the surf and sea town of the shore lord

occasion.words: நலம் தொலைந்தது எனத் தலைவனைத் தோழி கூறி வரைவு கடாயது

396.reading: To the man of the hill where the cloud that has rained rests on the peak, the falls roar on the honey-hung heights, and on the good day when the vengai decks the mountain a lovely peacock, having nosed through its gold-like flowering boughs and bathed in its pollen, drinks the young sunlight with its flock on the rock, the friend says she has no one to tell the grievous sickness his chest has caused; for many days he spoke lovely words and called himself her protection, and now he has lost his way without grace.
396.nuance: The peacock dusted with vengai pollen basking in the morning sun is the content the girl had expected; it carries a mood and no act, so it stays scene.

colophon.thurai: தோழி தலைமகனை வரைவு கடாயது வரைவு உணர்த்தப்பட்டு ஆற்றாளாய்ச் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம் இரவுக்குறி மறுத்ததூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: vengai, peacock and mountain

thurai_akam.speaker: thozhi
thurai_akam.note: the colophon does not name the speaker of this alternative

397.reading: The woman tells the friend who comforts her that her arms waste as the days go by, her eyes, gazing at the long waste road, have lost their light, her mind has left her and become something else, the sickness grows and evening has come; she does not fear dying, but fears that if in death she is born into another life she may forget her lover.
397.nuance: The fear is precise: not death, not the next birth as such, but the forgetting a new birth would bring.

colophon.thurai: பிரிவிடை ஆற்றாளாகி நின்ற தலைமகளை வற்புறாநின்ற தோழிக்கு ஆற்றுவல் என்பது படச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: the woman wasting while he is away on the waste road

398.reading: The friend tells the man leaving the day tryst that the fearsome god has withdrawn, the sun of spreading rays bends west, and the girls of the oorai game, hair wet from the waves and bellies heaving, have gone home; when they praised the fragrant grove and said to the girl 'let us go ahead', she answered only a few words, and her young breasts were wet as her lovely flower-like eyes filled with tears.
398.nuance: Everything else has gone home in order; the friend reports the girl's silence and tears so that the man will be the one to console her, and by marrying her.

colophon.thurai: முன்னுற உணர்ந்து பகற்குறி வந்து மீளும் தலைமகனை நீ தான் இவளது தன்மையை ஆற்றுவி எனச் சொல்லியது

thinai_evidence.note: sunset on the sea beach

iraicchi.act: the tusker guards from behind his mate and the calf she has just borne
iraicchi.sense: the man will come to wed her and guard her and their household as the tusker guards his own

399.reading: The friend, with the man listening, tells the girl that her bright brow's beauty will show she has the worth for which the lord of the great hill comes desiring her, the hill where by roaring falls the blood-red kaanthal opens for striped-winged bees, and on the plantain slope a young she-elephant that has calved rests with her calf in the gleam of gems a boar dug up, while the tusker guards them from behind.

colophon.thurai: நெடுங்காலம் வந்து ஒழுக ஆற்றாமை வேறுபட நின்ற தலைமகளைத் தோழி எம்பெருமான் இதற்காய நல்லது புரியும் என்று தலைமகன் சிறைப்புறத்தானாகச் சொல்லியது இதற்காய நல்லது புரியும் பெருமான் திறம் வேண்டும் என்றாட்குத் தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉம் ஆம்

thinai_evidence.note: kaanthal, boar and tusker of the hill

comparisons.tenor: his unfailing place in her heart

400.reading: The courtesan tells the lord of the town, where by paddy fields with plantain leaves bending low the great dark-backed vaalai leaps beside the sheaves the reapers have laid, that if she could do without him she would stay here and gain something by sulking; but bound with a rare friendship, he knows no failing in her heart, just as justice never fails in the Uranthai court of the warlike Cholas.
400.nuance: Her praise is also a renunciation of oodal: she cannot even sulk at him, because his place in her heart is as fixed as an institution.

colophon.thurai: பரத்தை தலைவனைப் புகழ்ந்தது முன்பு நின்று யாதோ புகழ்ந்தவாறு எனின் நின் இன்று அமையாம் என்று சொன்னமையான் என்பது நற்றிணை முற்றும்

thinai_evidence.note: paddy fields, vaalai fish and the town lord

links.note: Purananuru 101: Avvai tells her heart that Athiyaman's gift, late or soon, is as sure as the food an elephant holds between its tusks. Natrinai 381 (also Avvaiyar): the rain has settled in like Neduman Anji's seat from which he keeps giving chariots.
links.teaches: The same poet who in puram counts on Anji's giving as something that never fails makes that unfailing giving the image of a rain a waiting woman cannot bear, so the patron's plenty is a blessing to the bard and a torment to the lover depending on who receives it.

links.note: Kural 1161: she would hide this pain, but it wells up like spring water when drawn. Natrinai 382: at evening she must hide her grief even if her life goes.
links.teaches: The couplet gives the woman's wish to hide her pain without a reason and says it fails; the Natrinai woman supplies the reason, that the slander of his enemies would shame him, so concealment in separation is shown to be a duty to his name and not only her modesty.

links.note: Kural 1102: other diseases have other cures, but the sickness this jewelled woman causes she alone cures. Natrinai 384: eloping, the man calls her the one who was the medicine when he suffered after casting off shame.
links.teaches: The Kural's paradox that the woman is the cure for the sickness she causes becomes in Natrinai 384 the eloping man's reason for taking her across the waste: he now carries his medicine with him, so the couplet's moment of union is extended into the whole journey of udanpokku.

links.note: Akananuru 175: the clouds flash more often than the spear Chezhiyan raised after his victory at Alankanam; the time he set for return has come. Natrinai 387: the cloud flashes like swords drawn in Chezhiyan's camp at Alankanam; he will come.
links.teaches: In both poems the lightning of the promised rains is measured by the weapons of Chezhiyan's victory at Alankanam, spoken once by the waiting woman and once by her friend, so the battle had become a stock sign of the season of return and could serve either as complaint (the time is here) or as comfort (he will come).

links.note: Akananuru 91: even if he won Kuttuvan's Kudanadu, he would not stay there forgetting her beauty. Natrinai 391: who would leave for wealth even to win Nannan's Ezhil hill, and make her eyes weep?
links.teaches: The friend's comfort had a fixed shape, a famous chief's rich land weighed against the woman's beauty or tears, and the pair shows its two stages: in the Akananuru the man has already gone and will not linger, in the Natrinai the journey is only announced and will not be made at all.

links.note: Akananuru 376: the courtesan tells the lord to give back her beauty, which was like Kuttuvan's Maranthai, and then go. Natrinai 395: the friend tells the shore lord to give back the girl's beauty, which is like Maanthai on the sea, and go.
links.teaches: The same formula, beauty likened to a Chera town and demanded back before he leaves, is spoken by a discarded courtesan in the Akananuru and by the friend of an unmarried girl here, so the restitution formula belonged to the speech of any woman wronged by the man, and in the friend's mouth it becomes a demand for marriage.

links.note: Kuruntokai 49 (Ammuvanar): even when this life changes to the next, may you be my husband and I the one close to your heart. Natrinai 397 (Ammuvanar): I do not fear death, but I fear that in another birth I may forget my lover.
links.teaches: The same poet gives the hope and the fear of the same belief: in Kuruntokai 49 rebirth is a chance to be joined again, in Natrinai 397 it is the risk of forgetting, so for these women the next birth mattered only as it kept or lost the present love.

links.note: Purananuru 39: because justice stands firm and unfailing in the Chola court at Uranthai, justice is not this king's own fame. Natrinai 400: like justice that never fails in the Uranthai court of the warlike Cholas, he knows no failing in her heart.
links.teaches: The puram poet says Uranthai's justice is too settled to count as any one king's merit, and the courtesan borrows exactly that settledness for her lover's place in her heart, so an inherited institution, not a person's virtue, was the akam poet's measure of a love that cannot change.

source_issues: 385 lines 7 and 8: the text breaks off (எழுது எழில் மழைக்க ...); the colophon has no thurai and no poet; marked from lines 1 to 6, uncertain.

386: the colophon thurai describes the friend appeasing a wife after the husband's return from a courtesan, a marutham situation, but the poem is kurinji and speaks of the man's oath and his coming to wed; recorded as given.
400: the colophon thurai ends with நற்றிணை முற்றும், the closing of the anthology, run into the thurai; copied as given.
